theme: Seeing a doctor about back pain
summary_zh: 學會轉述醫生、家人給你的建議：suggest／recommend + V-ing 或 that + 原形、insist on + V-ing、deny + V-ing，把看診經過說清楚。

vocab.definition: to suddenly hurt the muscles in your lower back
vocab.example: Bend your knees when you lift that box, or you'll throw out your back.
vocab.example_zh: 搬那個箱子時膝蓋要彎，不然你會閃到腰。

vocab.definition: a sudden, sharp pain that seems to travel along part of your body
vocab.example: I sometimes get a shooting pain down my left leg when I stand up.
vocab.example_zh: 我站起來的時候，有時候左腿會一陣刺痛。

vocab.definition: hard to move or bend, and often painful
vocab.example: My neck is always stiff after a long flight.
vocab.example_zh: 長途飛行之後，我的脖子總是很僵硬。

vocab.definition: the way you hold your body when you sit or stand
vocab.example: Bad posture at your desk can cause back and neck pain.
vocab.example_zh: 坐在辦公桌前姿勢不良，可能會造成背痛和脖子痛。

vocab.definition: treatment for injuries using exercise, stretching and massage
vocab.example: After the injury, she had physical therapy twice a week for two months.
vocab.example_zh: 受傷之後，她做了兩個月的物理治療，每週兩次。

vocab.definition: a medical office where you can see a doctor without booking first
vocab.example: There's a walk-in clinic next to the station, so you won't need an appointment.
vocab.example_zh: 車站旁邊有一家免預約的診所，所以你不需要先掛號。

vocab.definition: designed to be comfortable and safe for the human body to use
vocab.example: The company gave everyone an ergonomic keyboard to prevent wrist pain.
vocab.example_zh: 公司發給每個人一個符合人體工學的鍵盤，預防手腕痛。

vocab.definition: the fixed amount you pay for a doctor's visit when insurance pays the rest
vocab.example: With my insurance, the co-pay for each visit is only twenty dollars.
vocab.example_zh: 有保險的話，我每次看診的部分負擔只要二十美元。

reading.title: A Pain in the Back
paragraphs: Last Monday, right after a handoff meeting about a new client account, Daniel bent down to pick up a heavy box of files and felt something pop in his lower back. At first he thought it was nothing. He took some over-the-counter painkillers and went back to his desk, but by the evening his back was so stiff that he could hardly stand up straight.

The next morning, his co-worker Mia suggested going to the walk-in clinic near the office instead of waiting a week to see his usual doctor. When Daniel said he was too busy because of a stakeholder meeting that afternoon, Mia insisted on driving him there herself during lunch.

The doctor asked a lot of questions. Daniel denied lifting anything heavy at the gym, but he admitted that he sat at his desk for about ten hours a day and rarely took breaks. The doctor said his posture was the real problem, and that the pain could easily flare up again if he didn't sort it out. She recommended that he start physical therapy twice a week, and she suggested taking a short walk every hour.

Daniel had been worried about the cost, but his co-pay was only twenty dollars. On the way back, he ordered an ergonomic chair, a big upgrade from the old one he had been using for years. Sitting properly has a learning curve, he admits, and he still slouches when he gets busy. But the shooting pain down his leg, which started a day after the injury, has already eased, and he has stopped letting unfinished work carry over into his evenings.

questions.q: Why did Daniel go to the walk-in clinic?
options: His usual doctor had closed the office.
Mia suggested it so he wouldn't have to wait a week.
The doctor at the gym told him to go there.
His company insisted on a health check after the meeting.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：Mia suggested going to the walk-in clinic… instead of waiting a week to see his usual doctor（不用等一週看平常的醫生）。

options: Lifting weights at the gym twice a week
Taking stronger painkillers every evening
Starting physical therapy twice a week
Working from home until the pain stops
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：She recommended that he start physical therapy twice a week，另外建議每小時走一走。

questions.q: What can we infer about the main cause of Daniel's back problem?
options: It was mostly caused by long hours of sitting with bad posture.
It was caused by an accident at the gym.
It started because the new chair was uncomfortable.
It was a side effect of the painkillers.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：他否認在健身房搬重物（denied lifting anything heavy at the gym），但承認每天坐十小時、很少休息，醫生也說 his posture was the real problem，可見主因是久坐和姿勢不良，搬箱子只是導火線。

grammar.point: Reporting verbs: suggest, recommend, insist on, deny
grammar.point_zh: 轉述動詞：suggest、recommend、insist on、deny 後面接什麼

guide.key_zh: 四個都接 V-ing（insist 要加 on）；suggest／recommend that 子句動詞用原形。

uses.note_zh: suggest 後面不接 to V，也不接「人 + to V」
不管主詞是誰都用原形：that he start、that she not lift
on 不能省；也可說 insist that + S + V
也可用 deny having + p.p.；不接 to V

mistakes.wrong: The doctor suggested me to take a break.
mistakes.right: The doctor suggested (that) I take a break.
mistakes.why_zh: suggest 不接「人 + to V」；要提到人就用 that + 人 + 原形

mistakes.wrong: My wife insisted to drive me there.
mistakes.right: My wife insisted on driving me there.
mistakes.why_zh: insist 後面要加 on，再接 V-ing

mistakes.wrong: He denied to lift the boxes.
mistakes.why_zh: deny 後面接 V-ing，不接 to V

examples.en: "Why don't you take a short walk every hour?" → The doctor suggested taking a short walk every hour.
examples.zh: 「你何不每小時走一走？」→ 醫生建議每小時散步一下。

examples.en: "You should start physical therapy." → She recommended that he start physical therapy twice a week.
examples.zh: 「你應該開始做物理治療。」→ 她建議他每週做兩次物理治療。

examples.en: "I'm driving you there. No arguments." → Mia insisted on driving him to the clinic.
examples.zh: 「我載你去，不准拒絕。」→ Mia 堅持要載他去診所。

examples.en: "I didn't lift anything at the gym." → Daniel denied lifting anything heavy at the gym.
examples.zh: 「我在健身房沒搬任何東西。」→ Daniel 否認在健身房搬過重物。

exercises.q: "Why don't you take short breaks?" → The doctor suggested ___ (take) short breaks every hour.
exercises.explain_zh: suggest 後面直接接動作時用 V-ing：suggested taking。

exercises.q: "You should see a physical therapist." → She recommended that he ___ (see) a physical therapist twice a week.
exercises.explain_zh: recommend that + 人 + 原形動詞；主詞是 he 也用原形 see，不是 sees 或 saw（英式也可說 should see）。

exercises.q: "I'm driving you to the clinic. No arguments." → My wife insisted ___ (drive) me to the clinic.
exercises.explain_zh: insist 後面要加 on，再接 V-ing：insisted on driving。

exercises.q: "I didn't lift anything heavy at the gym." → Mark denied ___ (lift) anything heavy at the gym.
exercises.explain_zh: deny 後面接 V-ing：denied lifting（也可用 having lifted 強調是之前的事）。

exercises.q: "Don't carry a heavy bag for a while." → The physical therapist recommended ___ (not / carry) a heavy bag for a while.
exercises.explain_zh: recommend + V-ing 的否定是把 not 放在 V-ing 前面：recommended not carrying。

exercises.q: "We need to take an X-ray before I give you anything stronger." → The doctor insisted ___ an X-ray before giving me anything stronger.
options: to take
on taking
on take
taking
exercises.explain_zh: insist 後面一定要有 on，on 是介系詞所以接 V-ing：insisted on taking。to take、taking 少了 on；on take 動詞沒有加 -ing。

review.point: Indirect questions: Could you tell me where…
review.point_zh: 間接問句：Could you tell me… 後面改成直述句順序

exercises.q: "When does the clinic open?" → Could you tell me when ___ (the clinic / open)?
exercises.explain_zh: 拿掉 does，把時態加回動詞：the clinic opens（單數主詞加 -s）。

exercises.q: "What did the doctor say?" → Do you know what ___ (the doctor / say)?
exercises.explain_zh: 拿掉 did，把過去式加回動詞：the doctor said。

exercises.q: "Is the pharmacy open on Sundays?" → Do you know ___ (the pharmacy / be) open on Sundays?
exercises.explain_zh: Yes/No 問句要加 if（或 whether），再用直述句順序：if the pharmacy is。

guide.key_zh: 問句接在 Could you tell me 後面要改回直述句：主詞在前，拿掉 do/does/did。

uses.label_zh: 有 be 動詞或助動詞（is／are／can／will／has）：移到主詞後面
uses.form: Could you tell me + where + S + is／will V
uses.note_zh: is／are／can／will／has 移到主詞後面，不留在疑問詞後面

uses.label_zh: 有 do/does/did：拿掉它，時態加回動詞
uses.form: Do you know + when + S + V／V-s／V-ed
uses.note_zh: do → 動詞用原形；does → 動詞加 s；did → 動詞改過去式

uses.label_zh: Yes/No 問題：前面加 if 或 whether
uses.form: Do you know + if + S + V
uses.note_zh: if 後面一樣是直述句順序

mistakes.wrong: Do you know what time does breakfast start?
mistakes.right: Do you know what time breakfast starts?
mistakes.why_zh: does 要拿掉，三單的 s 加回 start

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me where is the meeting room?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me where the meeting room is?
mistakes.why_zh: 間接問句不倒裝：is 要放到主詞 the meeting room 後面

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me is the gym open 24 hours?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me if the gym is open 24 hours?
mistakes.why_zh: Yes/No 問題要加 if，而且 is 要放回主詞後面

listening.title: What Seems to Be the Problem?

lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I think I threw out my back yesterday, and it's been getting worse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Is it a dull ache, or more of a shooting pain?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Mostly a dull ache in my lower back, but sometimes there's a shooting pain down my left leg.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: Have you been taking anything for it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Just some over-the-counter painkillers. They help for a few hours, but then the pain comes right back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: Lifting heavy things is the classic way to throw out your back. Did you lift anything at the gym?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: No, honestly. It was a box of files at work. But I do sit at my desk for about ten hours a day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Dr. Lin

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel

lines.speaker: B

questions.q: Where does Daniel feel the pain?
options: Only in his left knee
In his neck and shoulders
In his lower back, and sometimes down his left leg
In his wrist from using the computer
questions.explain_zh: Daniel：Mostly a dull ache in my lower back, but sometimes there's a shooting pain down my left leg.

options: Physical therapy twice a week for a month

An X-ray before doing anything else
Going back to the gym every day
questions.explain_zh: Dr. Lin：I'd recommend physical therapy twice a week for a month，另外建議每小時起來走一走。

questions.q: Why does Daniel hesitate when he hears the doctor's advice?
options: He thinks the pain will go away on its own.
He is worried about finding time because of work.
He doesn't believe his posture is a problem.
He wants to see a different doctor first.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：他一聽到 Twice a week? 就說 I've got a big stakeholder meeting this afternoon, and the rest of the month is packed，可見他擔心工作太忙排不出時間。

dictation: They help for a few hours, but then the pain comes right back.
Your muscles are stiff, and your posture isn't helping.

shadowing: The doctor suggested taking a short walk every hour.

prompts.question: A friend has a stiff neck from working on a laptop all day. What would you suggest? Answer in one or two sentences.
prompts.question_zh: 朋友整天用筆電工作，脖子很僵硬。你會給什麼建議？用一兩句話回答。
hints: I'd recommend that you + V（原形）…
prompts.sample: I'd suggest raising your laptop to eye level, and I'd recommend that you take a short break every hour.

prompts.question: The last time you were sick, what did a doctor or someone in your family tell you to do? Report it in one or two sentences.
prompts.question_zh: 上次生病時，醫生或家人叫你做什麼？用一兩句話轉述。
prompts.sample: When I came down with the flu last winter, the doctor suggested staying home for three days, and my wife insisted on making me soup every night.

writing.task: You saw a doctor about back pain caused by long hours at your desk. Write a short message to your manager explaining what the doctor said and how it will affect your schedule this month.
writing.task_zh: 你因為久坐造成腰痛去看了醫生。寫一封簡短的訊息給主管，說明醫生說了什麼，以及這個月的行程會受到什麼影響。
writing.sample:
Hi Karen,

I saw a doctor yesterday about my back. She said the pain comes mainly from sitting for too long, and she recommended that I start physical therapy twice a week for a month. The sessions are on Tuesday and Friday mornings, so I'll start work at ten on those days and stay a bit later to make up for it.

She also suggested getting up and walking around every hour, so please don't worry if you see me pacing during calls. My wife has already insisted on setting a reminder on my phone, so I don't think I'll forget.

Thanks for understanding,
Daniel
checklist_zh: suggest／recommend 後面用 V-ing，或 that + 人 + 原形動詞
insisted 後面有加 on，再接 V-ing
說清楚對行程的影響（哪幾天、幾點）
語氣禮貌、精簡，一段講一件事

reading.title: The Perfect Posture Is a Myth
paragraphs: For decades, office workers have been told to sit up straight: feet flat on the floor, shoulders back, screen at eye level. Workplace guides insisted on it, and generations of parents nagged their children about slouching. Yet a growing number of physical therapists now argue that the idea of a single "correct" posture is, at best, an oversimplification.

Their reasoning is surprisingly simple. The spine is built to move, not to hold one position for hours on end. Even a textbook-perfect posture becomes a strain if you stay frozen in it all afternoon. As one therapist put it, "Your best posture is your next posture." In other words, the problem isn't so much how you sit as how long you sit without shifting.

This doesn't mean posture is irrelevant. Hunching over a laptop for ten hours a day will eventually take its toll, and someone recovering from an injury may need to be more careful. But an obsession with getting every angle right can backfire. People who worry about sitting "wrong" often tense up, which can make the very pain they are trying to avoid even worse.

So what do the experts recommend instead? Mostly unglamorous habits: getting up every half hour, taking calls on your feet and building short walks into the day. Some suggest setting a timer; others recommend drinking more water, partly so that trips to the kitchen become unavoidable. None of this requires an expensive chair, although a decent one certainly doesn't hurt.

The message, in short, is to stop chasing perfection and start chasing variety. Your back, it turns out, cares far less about how you sit than about whether you ever stand up, walk around and give it a change of position.

questions.q: What does "Your best posture is your next posture" mean?
options: You should keep changing position instead of holding one.
You should copy the posture of the person next to you.
Your posture will naturally improve as you get older.
You should practice one perfect position until it feels easy.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段緊接著解釋：the problem isn't so much how you sit as how long you sit without shifting——重點是常換姿勢，不是找到一個完美姿勢。

questions.q: Why might worrying too much about posture make back pain worse?
options: People stop exercising completely.
Anxious people tend to tense their muscles.
They buy chairs that are the wrong size.
They sit with their feet off the floor.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段說擔心坐錯的人 often tense up（肌肉繃緊），反而讓想避免的疼痛更嚴重。

questions.q: What can we infer is the real purpose of drinking more water?
options: To lose weight while working
To avoid getting a headache
To force yourself to get up more often
To replace coffee during the day
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第四段說多喝水 partly so that trips to the kitchen become unavoidable——讓你不得不起身走去廚房，真正目的是多動。

questions.q: What is the writer's view of expensive ergonomic chairs?
options: They are the best way to prevent back pain.
They can help, but they are not essential.
They usually make posture worse.
They are only useful for people with injuries.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：None of this requires an expensive chair, although a decent one certainly doesn't hurt——不是必要，但有一張好椅子也無妨。

listening.title: No Couch for a Week

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: So, uh, the physical therapist says I basically need to stop sitting so much. Easier said than done.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Wait, did she say anything about the chair? The one you insisted on buying—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: The ergonomic one, yeah. She said it's fine, but it's not some magic fix.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Huh. So we spent four hundred dollars on a nice-to-have.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Well, I wouldn't put it like that. It's way more comfortable, and I've already—

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Okay, okay, I'm just teasing. What else did she suggest?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Setting a timer to go off every thirty minutes and taking calls standing up. Oh, and she recommended that I stop working on the couch at night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Ha! I've been saying that for months. Did she give you any exercises?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Yeah, a whole sheet of stretches. Ten minutes every morning, no excuses.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Then I'm holding you to it. Skip one, and it's no couch for a week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: That's a bit harsh, isn't it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Maybe. But you're the one who's been limping around the kitchen since Monday.

questions.q: What did the physical therapist say about the ergonomic chair?
options: It was the main cause of his pain.
It's fine, but it won't solve the problem by itself.
He should return it and get a cheaper one.
It's the most important part of his treatment.
questions.explain_zh: Daniel：She said it's fine, but it's not some magic fix——椅子不錯，但不是萬靈丹。

questions.q: What can we infer about Grace's opinion of Daniel working on the couch?
options: She has thought it was a bad habit for a long time.
She only just found out about it.
She thinks it's better than working at a desk.
She wants to buy him a new couch.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她一聽到物理治療師建議不要在沙發上工作，就說 Ha! I've been saying that for months，可見她早就覺得這是壞習慣。

dictation: She said it's fine, but it's not some magic fix.
But you're the one who's been limping around the kitchen since Monday.

(for hours/days on end) continuously, without stopping

glossary.zh: 造成損害、帶來負面影響

to have the opposite result from the one you wanted

glossary.zh: 有了不錯但非必要的東西
